name: Orient yourself without GPS
blurb: A set of rough-and-ready methods for finding direction with nothing but the sun, a watch, a stick and some attention to your surroundings.
gear: An analogue watch or the willingness to imagine one
steps: Learn the shadow-stick method: mark the tip of a stick’s shadow, wait 15 minutes, mark it again — the line between them runs roughly west to east.
Learn the watch method for your hemisphere: in the north, point the hour hand at the sun and bisect the angle to the 12.
Learn the sun’s daily arc: it rises broadly east, sets broadly west, and is due south at local noon in the northern hemisphere.
Learn to find north at night from Polaris via the Plough, or south from the Southern Cross.
Use terrain association: rivers run downhill to bigger water, ridge lines and roads are handrails.
Practise by predicting the direction of home from an unfamiliar spot, then checking with a compass.
tips: Moss on the north side of trees is unreliable folklore. Use the sun and stars.
These methods give you a general direction, not a bearing. Treat them as a sanity check, not a route.
proof: You correctly identify north within about 15 degrees, by day and by night, without instruments.
